title: Self-picked backlog
prompt: Work through BACKLOG.md: give every coder the whole list and let each coder pick its own next task.
starter: scripts/lab/scenarios/backlog/starter (todokit from qb9's sim/board-ab starter2: store + command registry + 30-task BACKLOG.md)
about: A to-do library with 30 tasks in one shared list, where coders pick their own work: 5 pairs of tasks are the same work worded far apart, some tasks need others first, and most touch the same few files.

profile.dependencyChain: helpers (dates, tags, format) -> commands that use them (add, due, overdue, groups)
profile.note: qb5; same starter and hidden tests as qb9's round-1 s2 (local claude -p): A built 3-4 of 5 pairs twice, E (dedupe) 0

anchors.note: no judge for this scenario (it measures waste, not quality); reference = qb9's round-1 finished repos, 30/30

title: Build a bakery website from scratch
prompt: Build a website for a small bakery: menu, opening hours, online orders.
starter: scripts/lab/scenarios/bakery/starter (a product brief in README.md, a stub server, one smoke test)
about: A whole small product from an empty repo: menu with allergens and stock, ordering into 15-minute pickup slots, cancelling, Portuguese pages, an owner's admin area with CSV export, and a JSON API. Sized so one agent needs a long time and many agents can split it.

profile.dependencyChain: storage + seed data -> API routes and validation -> pages and admin pages -> tests
profile.note: first guesses by qb5; greenfield: all work starts from one stub file, so early tasks collide on server.js unless the plan sets up structure first

anchors.note: one Opus agent built the reference in ~13 min

title: Make the café family-friendly
starter: scripts/lab/scenarios/cafe-family/starter (Corner Café: the demo seed with its 14 tasks applied)
about: A vague feature request on a small existing website: the planner has to decide what family-friendly means and split it into changes.

profile.note: first guesses by qb5; replace with measured values after stage 1

title: Build a padel club app
prompt: Build a booking app for a padel club.
starter: scripts/lab/scenarios/club/starter (foundations in lib/, modules/ empty, the brief in README.md, 3 tests)
about: The stage-2 big job: a wide product on ready-made foundations (storage, sign-in, courts, slots, prices, wallet, layout). 13 independent modules: bookings, member area, public pages, waitlist, notifications and calendar, blocks, coaches and lessons, tournaments, staff admin, reports, pro-shop, staff rota, each in English and Portuguese. A wide job with a shallow chain: the honest best case for many agents.

profile.dependencyChain: foundations (in the starter) -> 13 modules, each on the foundations only; waitlist, calendar and reports also read bookings/lessons -> depth 2 at most
profile.note: qb5; measured 2026-10-08: one Opus subagent finished the whole brief in 881 s (14.7 min), far under the ~60-min target

anchors.note: one Opus subagent built the reference in 14.7 min (one session); reference without the judge: 100

title: Port a library to TypeScript
about: 48 string validators from validator.js 13.12.0 (MIT), plain JavaScript with no official TypeScript version: every module has to become typed TypeScript without changing what it does.

profile.dependencyChain: util/assertString, util/merge -> isFQDN, isIP, isByteLength -> isEmail, isURL; src/index last
profile.note: first guesses by qb5; replace with measured values after stage 1

anchors.note: reference without the judge: 100; a Sonnet agent ported it

title: Two teams, one repo
prompt: Team A: work through TEAM-A.md; give every coder the whole list and let each coder pick its own next task.
starter: scripts/lab/scenarios/two-teams/starter (todokit, BACKLOG split into TEAM-A.md T1-T15 and TEAM-B.md T16-T30)
about: Two teams, each with its own list of 15 tasks, change one to-do library at the same time. Their lists overlap in meaning, not words: five tasks in team B ask for what team A builds under other names.

profile.dependencyChain: team A helpers -> team B commands and twins (cross-team)
profile.note: qb5; all 5 duplicate pairs and several dependencies cross the teams, so only something both teams see (the board) can catch them

anchors.note: no judge; shares backlog's hidden tests
